Issued at 1105 PM CDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Earlier this evening an upper level trough was lifting 
northeast across western Kansas. Lingering showers/sprinkles 
continue across southwest Kansas ahead of this upper wave given 
the lingering layer of deep low level moisture and weak lift. 
As this upper wave continues to move east/northeast overnight 
the light precipitation will taper off, however cloud cover is 
expected to linger into Sunday. This is due to the slow west to 
east erosion of the deep moist layer. In the areas the do break 
out overnight these locations will quickly have fog/stratus 
develop given the moist upslope flow. Currently the latest 
guidance indicates that this fog will reduce visibilities to 
less than 1 mile west of highway 83 but the probability of the 
dense fog from the ensembles are around 50 percent and mainly 
near the Colorado border. Given this limited area and low 
confidence have at this time opted to not issue a dense fog 
advisory. Will however monitor this closely and issue one later 
tonight if required. Despite not issuing a dense fog 
advisory....anyone traveling near the Colorado border should be 
prepared for patchy dense fog. 

Thunderstorm chances will increase Sunday night across 
southwest Kansas. A few storms will be capable of producing 
gusty winds of 50 mph or higher. On Sunday an upper level trough
will deepen as it crosses the southwest United States. Across 
eastern Colorado during the day the surface pressures will begin
to fall as a result of this deepening upper level trough 
approaching from the west. This will result in increasing 
southerly winds which will draw gulf moisture back across west 
Texas into eastern Colorado and southwest Kansas. Sunday night 
an upper level disturbance embedded in the moist southwest flow 
ahead of this main upper trough will approach southwest Kansas 
and as it does scattered evening thunderstorms developing over 
northeast New Mexico and eastern Colorado. What storms that do 
develop will spread into southwest Kansas overnight as the 
eastern Colorado surface boundary moves eastward into western 
Kansas. A few of these elevated storms overnight may be capable 
of producing wind gusts of 50 mph or a little higher given the 
improving downdraft cape and 0-6km shear along 850-700mb 
moisture transport/warm air advection developing across 
southwest Kansas. 

A slight risk for severe thunderstorms will be possible Monday 
afternoon and evening east of highway 183. On Monday the main 
upper level trough will approach southwest Kansas during the day
as the Sunday night upper level disturbance exits western 
Kansas. As our more significant upper trough approaches, a cold
front will move into western Kansas. The surface trough of low 
pressure which will be moving across southwest Kansas Sunday 
night is now forecast to be located in south central Kansas near
Pratt and Medicine Lodge late day as the cold front crosses 
southwest Kansas. As this cold front intersects this surface 
boundary over south central Kansas late day the low level 
moisture convergence/lift will improve as the upper level 
synoptic lift increases in this area based on the location of 
the left exit region of an upper level jet. This will not only 
increase the chance for late day thunderstorms across south 
central Kansas near this boundary but also given the moisture 
return, shear and mid level instability now forecast in this 
area there will be a chance that few of these developing storms 
late day/early evening to be severe. Large hail and strong 
damaging winds will be the main hazards. Currently the exact 
location of where this boundary will be late Monday is still 
unclear with several of the ensembles placing it east of Pratt 
and Medicine lodge. At this time given uncertainty on the exact 
locations of the surface boundary and timing of the cold front 
moving into south central Kansas am currently unable to 
completely rule out the chance for a few severe storms east of 
highway 183 as the SPC slight risk highlights. Still with this 
said I also would not not be surprised if Monday afternoon 
storms develop near the Pratt and Medicine Lodge area and then 
move east of this area before becoming severe. 

Very windy conditions will be possible Monday night and Tuesday
as showers and thunderstorms continue across southwest Kansas.  
Further west of the late day convection potential over south 
central Kansas mention above there will also be additional 
thunderstorm activity near the 700-500mb deformation that will
be moving into western Kansas. As the main upper trough crosses
western Kansas Monday night this deformation zone will cross
southwest Kansas from west to east and produce another round 
(50-70% chance) of thunderstorms Monday night into early 
Tuesday. Very windy conditions will also accompany with this 
precipitation given the tight surface pressure gradient that
